questions.question: According to the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease (ICBD), how many points are assigned to genital aphthosis, and why is this specific finding critical for distinguishing Behçet's from other causes of aseptic meningitis in a patient with oral ulcers?

In a patient presenting with fever, headache, and hyponatremia, what specific combination of serum osmolality, urine osmolality, and volume status confirms the diagnosis of SIADH while ruling out hypovolemic hyponatremia or cerebral salt wasting?

Given that brain MRI was normal in this case of acute neuro-Behçet's disease, what cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings support the diagnosis of parenchymal-sparing acute neuro-Behçet's (aseptic meningitis phenotype) versus viral meningoencephalitis?
What is the proposed pathophysiological mechanism linking central nervous system inflammation in acute neuro-Behçet's disease to the development of SIADH, specifically regarding cytokine mediation?

While high-dose corticosteroids are the standard first-line therapy for acute neuro-Behçet's disease, what unique outcome was observed in this case with colchicine monotherapy, and how does this challenge current treatment paradigms for neurological involvement?

Beyond neurological symptoms, what two distinct clinical manifestations of severe hyponatremia were present in this patient that served as clues to the severity of the electrolyte disturbance before the diagnosis of SIADH was fully confirmed?

Why is HLA-B51 positivity considered supportive but not diagnostic for Behçet's disease, and how should a negative HLA-B51 result influence the diagnostic workup in a patient meeting clinical criteria?

In the context of this case, why was the elevation of soluble interleukin-2 receptor (sIL-2R) deemed non-specific, and what pitfalls exist when using this marker to screen for CNS lymphoma in patients with active systemic inflammation?
